newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria GIA names Afghan fighter as leader.
newsitem.headline: Algeria GIA names Afghan fighter as leader.

text.p: Algeria's feared rebel group, the Armed Islamic Group (GIA), has appointed a veteran of the Afghan war as its leader, the Arabic-language newspaper Asharq al-Awsat said on Thursday.
The newspaper said the GIA issued a statement on Wednesday announcing Slimane Mehrezi, 36, had replaced Antar Zouabri.
Zouabri had taken over after leader Jamal Zitouni was killed in a power struggle last July, according to Algerian security forces.

The newspaper gave no details on the fate of Zouabri, who last month dismissed Algerian outrage at the killing of civilians, saying "there are many religious proofs which make legitimate (our) bombing operations even when there are civilian victims."

Asharq al-Awsat said: "Two issues divide GIA members. The first is related to strategy initiated by Zitouni which was followed by Zouabri which aims at killing family members of GIA former members who have surrendered to the authorities...Recent attacks on civilians come within this strategy."
Some GIA members opposed this policy, saying it would lead to the formation of splinter groups seeking revenge.
The newspaper said another divisive issue was whether the GIA should seek to merge its leadership with the Islamic Salvation Army (AIS), the armed wing of the outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS).

The FIS was Algeria's most powerful opposition party, taking a huge lead in a general election scrapped by the authorities in January 1992. Violence started shortly afterwards, with hardline FIS members setting up the AIS, with the GIA emerging later as the more ruthless of the two armed groups.
Some 60,000 people have been killed in the five-year-old conflict between Algerian security forces and Moslem guerrillas.
